newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES EASE WITH LACK OF ENQUIRIES.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES EASE WITH LACK OF ENQUIRIES.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel barge prices eased a little late on Wednesday as buyers bit by rising prices suddenly disappeared from the market, traders said.
But cargoes continued to be talked at strong numbers, they added.

After early deals at $96.50 and $96.75 fob ARA, high sulphur fuel oil barges traded at $95.75 and $95 in the late afternoon, with the latter some 50 cents below Tuesday's lowest trades. A few traders said deals were also done as low as $94.25.
"There's more sellers than buyers," one trader said.
"Prices were strong this morning but in the afternoon they fell a little with two trades at $95 (a tonne). I think it has to do with the lack of bunker enquiries," a second trader said.
"Most enquiries were postponed until tomorrow as the buyers felt that with every one looking for product the prices were going higher and higher," the trader added.
Other traders, however, said that the lower trades were done by market players trying to push prices down.
The higher barge prices witnessed recently -- levels not seen in several months -- were said to be the result of low offerings of prompt material from refiners and loading delays at two key sites.
High sulphur cargoes were quiet, but were notionally assessed steady with offers heard at $93/$94 cif and bids at about $91.
Some traders said that Russian cracked M-100 was being offered at premia of $2.50 to $3.50 over the two means quote.
One percent was assessed stronger on the back of rising swaps and with fewer avails on the market.
One seller said he was offering early in the day at a floating price but later withdrew his offer, pegging low sulphur cargoes at higher than $96.
"People want to sell at $97, the level of swaps," one trader said.
Low sulphur barges were also offered higher, with some sellers asking as high as $98 but little buying interest was seen.
